  "relation": "REFINED",
  "consensus_summary": "Consensus treats ‘bow’ (qeshet) as dual: primarily the war-bow of military power/warfare/judgment (broken bow = end of war or humbling of might) or the rainbow as covenant mercy/faithfulness (Gen 9), with frequent recognition that the same word covers both and that tradition often links them (rainbow as God’s unstrung/reversed war-bow).",
  "book_summary": "The bow is what strings a people together—the kingdom’s covenant together with the might that is that covenant’s outward face; one word carries weapon, might and covenant-token, so that to break the bow is to unstring the kingdom.",
  "consensus_core_identification": "Dual distinct referents of qeshet: war-bow (power, warfare, judgment) or rainbow (covenant sign), optionally linked.",
  "book_core_identification": "Single unified reality of kingdom-binding covenant-and-might (weapon as outward face of the covenant-token).",
  "core_relation": "COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP",
  "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION",
  "boundary_disagreement": "Consensus keeps weapon and rainbow as separable primary senses (with optional linking) and admits further alternatives (personal strength, family quiver, white-horse conquest, deceitful bow, or even the verb ‘to bow’); the book collapses weapon/might and covenant-token into one inseparable kingdom-stringing referent and re-reads breaking the bow as unstringing the kingdom itself.",
  "material_contradiction": "None; the book synthesizes the consensus dual senses rather than denying either.",
  "rationale": "Minimum cores overlap on the dual content of qeshet (weapon/might + covenant) and on the broken-bow motif.   "citation_support": "PARTIAL",
  "strongest_objection": "The Noahic rainbow is a universal creation covenant, not a particular kingdom’s military might, so the book’s forced political unification may over-extend the shared Hebrew word beyond the distinct contexts the consensus rightly keeps separate.",
